recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. No further FHIR-core source work is needed for FHIR-39433; any additional IPA-specific conformance guidance belongs in IPA, and actor-specific CapabilityStatement discovery is covered by later ActorDefinition work rather than by changing implementationGuide.
issue_request: FHIR-39433 was a Published FHIR-core change request resolved Not Persuasive with Modification. It asked FHIR-I to consider IPA guidance around CapabilityStatement.implementationGuide and CapabilityStatement.instantiates; the final decision rejected the IPA interpretation that implementationGuide means all of an IG while instantiates means partial support, and instead required a clarifying note on CapabilityStatement.implementationGuide.
initial_application: FHIR-30587 first added a terse note that implementationGuide is primarily for IGs without role-specific CapabilityStatements and that instantiates should identify supported roles. Commit 92f8ebd5cf32bb1e6d497a86b5bb3e8306e3aef3 explicitly applied FHIR-39433 by replacing that note with the current fuller clarification in source/capabilitystatement/structuredefinition-CapabilityStatement.xml.
additional_context: source/fhir.ini lists CapabilityStatement as an active resource, so the StructureDefinition source is in current build scope. The IPA-origin issue FHIR-35321 explains the background use of instantiates in IPA. Later FHIR-42975 was resolved No Change because CapabilityStatement.implementationGuide already says it is not for IGs that define their own CapabilityStatements; actor-specific discovery was handled separately by FHIR-43899.
reconciliation: No source change was made. The current CapabilityStatement.implementationGuide comment already says that implementationGuide asserts adherence to IG-level global definitions and textual requirements, does not assert conformance to CapabilityStatements defined in the IG, and that CapabilityStatement.instantiates is required to assert conformance to those CapabilityStatements.
